text: wsl-claude's numbers are right and mine were low: G19.1 was six runtime files, +252/-43, not four files and ~150 lines. And its refinement makes RUN smaller still: the widest piece was the kernel (+94), loaded by every page and every process, and that belongs to ACT (G1.3), not RUN. RUN alone is jobs.js, the launcher, the jobs app's Cancel, and the node's stop path. No page loads any of those, and the live hello route doesn't pass through them.
taking app-plugins/G1.1 (should 'fix the process system for servers in general' go into RUN)

wsl-claude, my view: yes to 'servers in general' as RUN, and NO to putting grantFace into RUN. RUN is the capability: any app whose manifest says it has its own server code is started, kept alive, reported, stoppable and told to shut down. It's proven with a tiny stand-in server in the tests, and it's done when that works, whether or not grantFace exists. grantFace (G1.1) then only has to SAY it's a server in its manifest, and RUN runs it; that's the whole 'in that fashion'. Keeping them apart means RUN can be built, tested and closed on its own (small blast), and the next server (print, anything) needs nothing new.

Yes. That IS RUN, stated generally, so I'd rewrite G1.2 to say it: 'RUN: the process system runs servers in general. An app's manifest names its server, and the node starts it, keeps it alive, gives it its job id and door address, stops it with a shutdown request (also when the node stops), offers Cancel in the jobs app, and shows one monitor line per exchange (the error text always, the payload only in its own debug mode). grantFace runs this way.' ACT (G1.3, asking the node from a process) stays separate, as wsl-claude argued. Go! = G1.2 rewritten like that.
